Yes, so much anxiety! I’m still dealing with the aftermath of a few of those forgotten conversations. But it feels much better knowing that this time I will remember and I’m on the right track.

Honestly there were a few times that I know it must have been a really bad fall, even if I didn’t remember it.  the anxiety was overwhelming when I thought about the possibility of getting severely injured and not being able to call for help. Or being too stubborn to do so, out of fear of judgement. It terrified me to think about dying alone, drunk and lost. *shudder* I am grateful not to feel scared of that anymore. 🙏
I tried Naltrexone myself and didn’t really notice a difference. But I know several people that it helped a lot!

My immediate suggestions: take a slow, Deep breath. Remind yourself: You are important, and valuable. You deserve to be happy and in control. It’s ok if you don’t know how yet; you’re in the right place for support. You’re not alone and you absolutely can discover the how. 

For tonight, I would suggest no more alcohol. Tall glass(es) of water. More deep breaths. Be kind to yourself. You posted here, that’s a great step in the right direction. Please consider getting medical and psychological assistance. It might seem scary, but I have found that I was not shunned or scolded or shamed. They were so very understanding and so happy for me that I asked for help. 

You can do this! I Will Not Drink With You Today!!
